author: vertedinde
body:
#### Description of Change

Following up on a great suggestion by @MarshallOfSound in #29377, this PR adds a function to our version bump script that changes the `support.md` file on two conditions:

1. When we promote a new major nightly version (i.e. 14.0.0-nightly.xx -> 15.0.0-nightly.xx)
2. When we promote a new major stable version (e.g. 14.x.x -> 15.0.0)

Ideally, we could simplify this to _only_ bump when a new nightly is created. The website bases it's public information off of the latest stable branch, so the currently supported versions will appear correctly as each nightly goes through the nightly -> stable cycle and eventually becomes stable.

However, I left in the new major stable bump for 1) backwards compatibility, so we don't need to manually update current nightly and beta, and 2) having an additional check before promoting a new stable release seems like a good safety check. 🙂

author: levshvarts
body:
shepherdmetricscollectioninterval setting was not handled correctly in shepherd - existing cluster workers would not be updated when the setting changed

I added proper handling of shepherdmetricscollectioninterval setting, such that each cluster worker would get updated with the new setting when it changes.
In addition, I changed what shepherdmetricscollectioninterval does - it dictates the interval at which metrics are pushed from shepherd to the controller. This should allow us to bring down the load on the regional influxDBs.
Since the behavior of shepherdmetricscollectioninterval in shepherd changed, I also introduces a command level argument to shepherd - `promScrapeInterval` which will direct the period at which shepherd now scrapes prometheus instances in each cluster(as well as envoy stats).
`promScrapeInterval` is a command line argument, since we should not be changing it explicitly, only for demos/debugs. In addition since I want an ability to control each of the cloudlet's scrape interval separately, I added several debug commands to update `promScrapeInterval`:
   - `set-scrape-interval`
   - `reset-scrape-interval`
   - `show-scrape-interval`

Mics changes:
   - var to const change for a bunch of things that should be constants
   - changed `assert` to `require` to unit-tests

author: taeold
body:
We move the logic for setting up environment variables for function instances from post-trigger parsing to pre-trigger parsing. This makes environment variables accessible during trigger parsing, e.g.

```
const myFunc = functions.runWith({minInstances: process.env.TIER == "PROD" ? 20 : 0})...
```

(Of course, there isn't a way for users to specify environment variables for now. That may change soon.)

This change simply refactors existing logic - nothing new is introduced and function deploys should work exactly as it is done today.

*Warning* There is technically a breaking change where we no longer pass caller's `process.env` when forking a process to parse function triggers in user's source code. We think this is removing what was previously an undefined behavior but recognize we may be breaking someone's workflow. We will soon propose a support for setting project-level environment variables more easily.

author: mattludwigs
body:
When the WatchDog would timeout due to inactivity, it would make a call
to itself to terminate while it was still processing the `:timeout`
message. This caused the shutdown process to never complete when
shutting down due to a timeout.

This fix allows the shutdown process to know if it should shutdown the
WatchDog server, in normal shutdown cases, or if it should allow the
WatchDog server to shut itself down.

author: aalear
body:
Played with adding smarter link paste support as described in #33. I'm not sure if fetching question titles is also a part of that issue, but that work will follow in a separate PR. If that's not necessary, then I think we could consider #33 fulfilled if/when this is merged.

In this PR:

- Detecting when something that looks like a URL is being pasted in and formatting that as a link.
    - No attempt to detect links within a larger body of pasted text. If the whole thing is a link, cool. If not, ah well.
- Pasting into code blocks is left to the default behaviour (or the code paste handler) to sort out.
- Pasting a URL into inline code will treat the pasted content as inline code within the same block.
    - Note that this deviates from how we treat pasting of anything else into inline code (which breaks up the inline code element), but I feel like making _that_ better in the long term is the way to go here. Happy to write it up as an issue if that'd help, but in the meantime I left a `TODO` comment.
- If any text is selected when a URL is pasted in, that text becomes the link text.

I don't know if there's a way to write some automated tests for this (I didn't see any for the code paste handler plugin either), but I tested manually and I'm pretty happy with where this is at. 🤞

author: adamhjk
body:
This PR fixes [ch1171]. The cause of this was that we used the component
state to record the condition we wanted the world to be in, and then we
would dispatch async functions that expect that world not to change when
they hit an await point. That assumption (an easy one to make) is wrong
- in fact, the data can, and does, sometimes change. The result was the
kind of "teleportation" we saw.

Unfortunately, it causes there to be an occasional "jitter" now when you
are moving a node around. I think I know the approximate cause (that the
calls are not resolved in order), but it's not a trivial fix. This
removes the big problem (things flying off the screen) for a smaller one
(nodes occasionally "jumping" for a split second sometimes).

body:
## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?
- [X] Bugfix
- [X] Feature
- [X] Documentation changes

## PR Checklist
For bug fixes / features, please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [ ] Testing has been carried out for the changes have been added
- [ ] Regression testing has been carried out for existing functionality
- [x] Docs have been added / updated

## What is the purpose of this PR?

At the moment this plugin doesn't deal with two new Notification Permissions statuses that have been added to iOS in v12 ("Provisional") and v14 ("Ephemeral"). 

This PR updates the plugin so that it does, and it also makes the default behavior such that if you are in either of those states, it will prompt the user for notification permissions when you call `requestRemoteNotificationsAuthorization`

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

At the moment when you call `requestRemoteNotificationsAuthorization` because these two permission states are not recognized, the system prompt for notifs is not shown. This PR changes that so the prompt is shown.

Happy to update the PR to make this optional or otherwise if needed.

## What testing has been done on the changes in the PR?
I've tested on iOS 14.6 with the `PROVISIONAL` and `NOT_DETERMINED` auth statuses, works as expected.

author: wpdolan
body:
We have implemented our planned functionalities described under the "Playerclass" section of our player interface implementation [plan](https://github.com/uchicago-cs/chiventure/wiki/Player-~-Interface-Implementation-Plan) as outlined in Issue #1057.

Changes Include:
- The addition of the  `copy_inventory` function to deep copy `skill_inventory_t` structs
-  Updates to the `player_set_class()` function and its corresponding test to also set the player's `player_stats`, `player_skills`, and `player_effects` fields when setting a player's class. These fields are deep copied with `copy_inventory()`, `copy_stat()` and `copy_effect()`
- Updates to `player_free()` to also free the newly deep copied `player_stats`, `player_skills`, and `player_effects` fields

Deep copying fields from the given `class_t` to the `player_t` when setting the class will allow for multiple players to be the same class without the risk of unintentionally modifying every player's stats/effects/skills when modifying the fields of a single player.

The remaining sections of the interface plan will be implemented into the player module in Issues #1053 and #1058.
